hypothesis: The production candidate outperforms the S&P 500 on TOTAL return (dividends reinvested) over a multi-year window
reason: The 8.55% benchmark quoted all week was price return; the objective specifies total return, and the gap is ~4 pts/yr not ~3. No configuration in this project beats SPY on total return. The candidate wins on drawdown, ruin, Sharpe and beta. Any claim of outperformance must name the dimension.
result: Decade: SPY total return 15.00% (Alpaca adjustment=all, 2016-01-04..2026-09-14, CONFIRMED) vs the candidate's ~9.9% parked (in-sample). Thirty years: SPY PRICE return 8.55% confirmed; total return ~10.3-10.6% ESTIMATED (no dividend-adjusted series available before 2016) vs candidate 5.75% parked. Every SPY-fraction blend measured 09-11 (25/50/75/100% of idle cash) also trails SPY on return. Risk-adjusted, confirmed on 7,719 aligned days: correlation 0.483, beta 0.205, vol 8.2% vs 19.2%, Sharpe 0.66 vs 0.52, maxDD -11.2% vs -56.5%; on SPY's ten worst days the candidate lost 0-1.2%.

hypothesis: The candidate's risk-adjusted advantage over SPY survives measuring Sharpe on EXCESS return over the 3-month bill rate (2.30% mean 1996-2026, 2.25% 2016-2026) rather than over zero
reason: Partly rejected. The advantage that survives is DRAWDOWN (Calmar 3.4x and 1.7x, maxDD -11.2% vs -56.5%/-33.8%, beta 0.205). On Sharpe and Sortino it is a tie: ahead over thirty years, at or behind SPY total return over the decade. 'Risk-adjusted outperformance' is true only if risk means drawdown.
result: 30yr: candidate parked Sharpe(excess) 0.53, Sortino 0.75, Calmar 0.51 vs SPY price 0.40/0.57/0.15 (SPY total return est. ~0.42 excess Sharpe). Decade: candidate alone 0.67/0.95/0.68 vs SPY TOTAL return 0.77/1.07/0.45. The rf=0 convention (0.87 vs 0.52) overstated the gap because 74% of the candidate's balance is cash earning rf, which a zero-rf Sharpe counts as risk-free alpha.

config.change: exit EXECUTION price only, not the exit decision

hypothesis: Rule exits fill at the session CLOSE (bar.close). Filling them nearer the session HIGH instead - same trades, same exit decision, better execution price - adds return without truncating any winner, which is what every previously rejected exit variant did.
reason: Registered before the result is known, per the research firewall. Distinct from EXP-0036 (11 exit variants, all rejected): those changed WHEN to exit and truncated winners; this changes only the fill price of an exit already decided.

config.event_date: peak news-coverage day each September, derived from the Alpaca news API rather than recalled

hypothesis: Buying a stock on its major product-launch news day and holding for the following days beats doing nothing, because the launch raises expected earnings (owner example: Apple iPhone launches).
reason: Registered before the result is known. The competing prior is buy-the-rumour-sell-the-news: a scheduled launch is among the most pre-priced events in markets, so the drift should land BEFORE the date and the event day should be at or near a local top.

config.events: 10 September launches 2016-2025, event day = peak news-coverage day derived from the Alpaca news API

hypothesis: RESULT for EXP-0040: buy a product launch on the day and hold.
reason: Buy-the-rumour-sell-the-news, confirmed on the owner example. The launch day is the wrong half of the trade: the first week after is negative on average and positive in only 3-4 of 10 years. n=10 is small and the +20d excess has wide error bars, but the direction is consistent and the mechanism (a scheduled, universally modelled event is priced before it happens) is causal. NOT wired into the money path.
result: Run-up (30 sessions BEFORE): mean +5.11%, median +6.06%, positive 9/10. Buying ON the day: +1d mean -0.58% (positive 3/10), +5d -0.33% (4/10), +10d +0.19% (4/10), +20d +0.78% (6/10). Excess over SPY: -0.89%, +0.01%, +1.23%, +1.49%. The pre-event drift is ~7x the 20-day post-event return.

config.measured_on: every trade the production candidate takes 1996-2026
config.note: supersedes EXP-0009, which bundled vol-targeting with regime and recorded no numbers

hypothesis: Trades entered while the MARKET is in a downtrend (SPY below its 200-day average, or SPY in drawdown) perform worse than those entered in an uptrend, so gating new entries on market regime would improve the book.
reason: Registered before the result. The competing prior is that this is already handled: each name must be above its OWN 200-day average to be bought, so in a bear market the candidate list empties by itself - which is why 2008 was only -8.1%. A market gate may be redundant with the per-name filter.

config.measured: all 1,501 production-candidate trades 1996-2026, bucketed by SPY state on the entry day

hypothesis: RESULT for EXP-0042: gate new entries on market regime (SPY downtrend).
reason: A market-downtrend gate would delete the bots best trades. It also settles the shorting question from the other side: the market falling is precisely when this books LONGS work hardest, so a short overlay would fight its own edge. SEPARATE CANDIDATE, not adopted: entries taken while SPY is within 2% of its high have median R 0.001 across 450 of 1,501 trades - 30% of all trades earning essentially nothing. Needs an ACCOUNT-level test before it means anything, because this project has repeatedly found per-trade quality rising while the account earns less. In-sample and contaminated.
result: REVERSED. Trades entered while the market is DOWN are BETTER, not worse. SPY below 200dma: mean R 0.183, median 0.230, win 54% (n=279) vs above: mean R 0.144, median 0.119, win 53% (n=1222). Below 50dma: mean R 0.211, median 0.289, win 56% (n=677) vs above 50dma: 0.103 / 0.055 / 52% (n=824) - roughly TWICE the edge per unit of risk. By SPY drawdown at entry: at highs (0 to -2%) mean R 0.059 median 0.001 (n=450, the WORST bucket); -2% to -5% mean R 0.316 median 0.414 win 61% (the best); -5/-10% 0.177; -10/-20% 0.071; worse than -20% 0.186.

hypothesis: EXP-0044: skipping entries while SPY is within X% of its high makes the ACCOUNT more money, since those 450 trades earn a median 0.001R.
reason: The same trap that has caught this project every time: per-trade quality rose and the account earned less. The near-high trades are not dead weight - they are low-yield deployment of capital that otherwise sits in bills at ~2.3%, and 30% of the trade count carries more of the compounding than its median R suggests. The parameter is kept, default None, as the documented record of a rejected idea.
result: REJECTED at every setting. baseline CAGR 5.75%, maxDD -11.2%, 1501 trades, 83.3% of years positive. skip within 1%: 4.65% / -11.4% / 1316. within 2%: 4.58% / -11.5% / 1151. within 3%: 4.46% / -12.3% / 1033. within 5%: 3.83% / -8.1% / 812. Monotonically worse on return as the gate tightens, and drawdown is WORSE at 1-3%, better only at 5% where return collapses by a third.

hypothesis: Stay invested on every day but let SIZE follow the edge: scale risk DOWN when SPY is within 2% of its high (median 0.001R) and UP during pullbacks (median 0.414R). Unlike EXP-0044 this never idles capital, it only reweights it.
reason: Registered before the result. Competing prior, from a sweep recorded in risk.py rather than the registry: raising risk_per_trade uniformly made every configuration worse - size multiplies edge and there is not much edge to multiply. This tests whether tilting size by regime is different from raising it everywhere.

hypothesis: BACK-FILL: raising risk_per_trade above 0.005 increases return.
reason: Migrated into the registry by the 2026-09-15 strategy audit, which found this was the ONLY live parameter with no registry entry. Predates the registry; the finding itself stands - size multiplies edge and there is not much edge to multiply.
result: Recorded in a code comment in risk.py, not in the registry until now: "Raising risk_per_trade instead made every configuration worse." The accompanying max_open_positions sweep at risk 0.005: 3 -> -0.69%, 6 -> +0.03%/+2.63%, 10 and 15 identical to 6 (the rule never finds more than ~10 simultaneous candidates).

hypothesis: RESULT for EXP-0045: tilt risk size by market regime.
reason: Not just lower return - DEEPER drawdown, and the mechanism is obvious in hindsight: up-sizing during a pullback means the largest positions are on precisely when the market keeps falling. EXP-0043 measured a higher edge per trade in those conditions, but edge per trade and drawdown are not the same quantity, and sizing into a falling market buys the second at the expense of the first. Together with EXP-0044 this closes the regime family: neither refusing to trade nor resizing beats sizing everything the same.

config.stops: excluded - a stop fills when hit, the price is not a choice

hypothesis: RESULT for EXP-0039: rule exits fill at bar.close; filling nearer the session high is worth something.
reason: The largest unclaimed prize measured on this project - bigger than the entry-timing change that shipped (+1.1). But it is a CEILING and must not be quoted as a gain: the day high is unknowable in advance, and the pullback rule that approximates it gives back its threshold (0.3%) by construction against an average available upside of only 0.60-0.97%. That eats a third to a half before anything is captured. Achievability needs the 5-minute test, not daily bars.
result: 30yr: baseline 5.17%; ceiling (every rule exit at that day HIGH) +221,030 -> 6.50% (+1.33 pts); half the range +110,515 -> 5.90% (+0.73). Decade: baseline 8.41%; ceiling 11.18% (+2.77); half 9.88% (+1.47). Both are LOWER bounds - the extra is added as terminal cash, not compounded from each exit. Average upside per share: reverted 0.60% of exit price (n=444), time_exit 0.97% (n=524), stop 0.00%.

config.fill: limit: at the level, or the open if gapped through

hypothesis: A real take profit - a resting limit at entry + N x risk - beats letting the RSI exit and the 20-day cap do the work. Owner: a target is smarter than waiting 20 days.
reason: Distinct from EXP-0036 mr_partial, which sold HALF at a level and cost 1.23 CAGR. This closes the WHOLE position and competes with the RSI exit, so it is a different question. Competing prior: 67% of all profit is in the top 50 trades and every holding-period test has been monotone in favour of holding longer, so a cap on the upside should cost more than it saves. Measuring rather than assuming.

hypothesis: RESULT for EXP-0049: a real take profit at N x the trade own risk.
reason: NOT a flat rejection, unlike the partial-profit variants. Return falls monotonically as the target tightens - 2.0R costs 0.10, 1.5R costs 0.60, 1.0R costs 0.87 - so any cap on the upside does cost money, as the top-50-trades-carry-67%-of-profit finding predicts. The 3.0R reading of +0.04 is 8 trades in 1,500 and is noise; do not adopt it. What IS real is 1.0R as a different point on the risk curve: -0.87 CAGR buys -2.1 points of drawdown, 3.4pp more positive years, and a worst year that moves from 2022 to 2008. Its CAGR-per-drawdown of 0.536 edges the baseline 0.513, though that gap is within noise and this is in-sample on contaminated data. A preference question for the owner, not a correctness one. Nothing enabled in production.

config.regime: SPY below/above its own 50-day average, from printed bars only
config.variants: both directions, because the data points the opposite way to the intuition

hypothesis: Owner's idea: one take-profit target is not right for every day. Take profit SOONER when the market is falling (bank it before it is taken back) and LATER when it is rising (let the good day run).
reason: The tension is measurable and worth naming before the result: EXP-0043 found roughly TWICE the edge per trade when SPY is below its 50-day average, so tightening the target on falling days cuts the best trades short. The owner intuition and the entry-side evidence disagree, so BOTH directions are run - tight-when-down and tight-when-up - rather than only the one expected to work.

hypothesis: RESULT for EXP-0051: should the take profit change with the market day?
reason: The owner was RIGHT about the direction and the entry-side inference was wrong to extrapolate: tightening the target on falling days costs 0.34 pts, tightening it on rising days costs 1.16. EXP-0043 measured the edge at ENTRY by regime; this shows that does not carry over to the EXIT day, which is a distinction worth keeping. But every variant still trails no-take-profit on return, and on CAGR-per-drawdown the baseline 0.513 is not beaten (best variant 0.512). What the owner version does buy is CONSISTENCY: 86.7% of years positive against 83.3%, for -0.34 CAGR and a marginally better drawdown. A preference trade, offered not adopted.
result: baseline 5.75% / -11.2% / 83.3% yrs+ve. OWNER DIRECTION (tight when market DOWN): 1R-down/3R-up 5.41% / -10.9% / 86.7%; 1R-down/none-up 5.43% / -11.0% / 86.7%; 1.5R-down/none-up 5.53% / -10.8% / 83.3%. INVERSE (tight when market UP): 3R-down/1R-up 4.59% / -10.2%; none-down/1R-up 4.56% / -10.2%; none-down/1.5R-up 5.20% / -11.0% / 80.0%. The owner direction beats the inverse by 0.82-0.87 CAGR pts.

hypothesis: P5: re-establish the frozen baseline after the Phase 1 correctness fixes (P2 participation cap, P3 exit-timing haircut).
reason: The exit-timing gap is worth about as much as the whole strategy edge, which nobody had priced. It is NOT a new cost - the bot has always sold at the trigger; the simulator was crediting it a close it never got. Every figure published before today was overstated by roughly 2.6 points. G13 passes (headline fell). The haircut is a conservative BOUND using the worst of three measured trigger times; the live distribution is UNVERIFIED pending ~30 logged rule exits, so the true drag is somewhere between the 0.120% case and this.
result: HEADLINE 5.75% -> 3.18% (-2.57 pts). Strategy alone 5.17% -> 2.19% (-2.98). Sharpe 0.53 -> 0.17, Sortino 0.75 -> 0.23, Calmar 0.51 -> 0.29, maxDD -11.2% -> -11.0%, years positive 83.3% -> 76.7%, trades 1522 -> 1501. P2 contributed ZERO (the 2% cap cannot bind below ~5m of equity against a 50m ADV floor); the entire move is P3. Arithmetic check: 980 rule exits / 30.7 yrs = 31.9/yr at ~15% position size x 0.652% = 3.12 pts predicted drag vs 2.98 observed.
